---
title: "Recipe: run the full garak baseline before sign-off"
toc-title: Recipe
---

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tool | [garak](https://docs.kailash.tools/reference/tools/garak.html) |
| Section | Scanning |
| Level | hard |
| Time | hours (full catalogue; plan per model) |
| Layer/Category | ATTACK / A-2 |
| Tags | `scan`, `baseline`, `garak`, `avid`, `regression` |

## Problem

The scoped scan answers one question cheaply (LLM01 here, data-leakage
there). A stack of single-question runs does not sign off a model. An
assessment needs the **full-catalogue baseline**. The baseline covers
every probe family. It uses one seed for reproducibility. It keeps the
raw JSONL. AVID reports are the hand-off artefact. Re-run the baseline
after every model, system-prompt or guardrail change. The diff is the
change's security statement.

## Solution

Budget a window (the full catalogue takes hours per model). Then run
the baseline end to end:

```bash
# 1. Confirm the pinned tool (Kailash ATTACK/A-2)
garak --version

# 2. Plan the spend: the catalogue is big — see what you are buying
garak --list_probes -v          # tiers + versions, no target needed

# 3. The full baseline (no --spec = the whole probe catalogue),
#    generous generations + a fixed seed + parallel headroom:
garak --target_type ollama --target_name <model> \
      -g 20 -s 1337 --parallel_attempts 16 \
      --report_prefix baseline-<model-tag>
```

What success looks like:

- the banner + `📜 reporting to baseline-<model-tag>_<timestamp>.jsonl`
  names THIS run's deliverable file
- per-probe progress lines end in per-detector pass/fail fractions
- the closing summary lists the weakest probes by detector score
- the run's JSONL (attempts + statuses) and the hit log stay in the
  working directory. They are the retained evidence

Convert and diff — the assessment hand-off and the regression loop:

```bash
# 4. AVID reports for the ticket/assessment
garak --report baseline-<model-tag>_<timestamp>.jsonl

# 5. The regression loop: after a system-prompt / guardrail / model change,
#    same seed, same target, new prefix:
garak --target_type ollama --target_name <model> \
      -g 20 -s 1337 --parallel_attempts 16 \
      --report_prefix retest-<change-tag>
garak --report retest-<change-tag>_<timestamp>.jsonl

# then compare per-probe detector scores across the two reports —
# what moved is what the change bought (or broke)
```

Expected output shape (abridged):

```
garak LLM safety & security scanning tool v<version> ( https://github.com/NVIDIA/garak ) at <ISO timestamp>
📜 reporting to baseline-<model-tag>_<timestamp>.jsonl
...
🔍 probing <probe> (<n> generation(s))
   <detector>  passed  <n>/<m>
...
✅ <n>/<m> probes passed / ❌ <k> failed (or the closing summary's shape)
```

## Discussion

- **Baseline vs scoped runs:** scoped runs answer questions
  (`--spec tag:…`, per-family specs). The baseline is the
  assessment-level evidence: one run, whole catalogue, before an
  assessment is signed off. In practice: full baseline first, scoped
  re-runs after every change. The same-seed diff does the day-to-day
  work.
- **Seeds are the experiment control:** `-s 1337` stays fixed across
  runs. It keeps the probe/target interaction set comparable. The
  report diff then states the change, not sampling noise. Change only
  one thing between runs.
- **Generations set the confidence:** `-g 20` suits a baseline;
  detector fractions stabilise. Use a higher value on gated models.
  Bootstrap confidence stats are available
  (`--confidence_interval_method bootstrap` with the `--bootstrap_*`
  knobs). Use them when a claim needs an interval, not a fraction.
- **`--parallel_attempts` is for API-tolerant targets:** hosted or
  local serving stacks that accept parallel load run much faster.
  Garak hints at the knob when the generator is parallel-capable.
  Keep the seed constant, so parallelism does not corrupt
  comparability.
- **The target endpoint is the blast-radius boundary:** run the
  server loopback on a lab box ([Serve a local model for
  scanning](../ops/serve-a-model.html)). Never point the baseline at a
  system outside the operator's control. The full catalogue is far
  more invasive than a scoped run.
- **Evidence retention:** keep the JSONL + hit log + the AVID
  conversion in the assessment record. Cite the ATLAS technique ids
  from the manifest row (AML.T0051/T0054, dataset-verified). Do not
  re-derive them. The
  [report-verification loop](../ops/report-verification-loop.html)
  recipe covers the full reporting discipline. It uses
  `--record`-based verbatim capture for anything that lands in a
  ticket.
